text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Black clouds gather in the United Nations proximity talks. U.N. special representative Han Sung-joo is expected to intervene "as a pilot" to switch their course.
- Health Minister Manolis Christofides rules out negotiations with doctors while they are on strike.
- Two men are charged in Paphos after an attack on two British tourists.
- A psychiatric patient pleaded guilty to two killings in the psychiatric hospital of Athalassa last year.
- Socialist Edek and Communist Akel parties express optimism there will be a positive conclusion to their talks exploring the possibility of cooperation in next year's presidential poll.
- Consultations between parties of the opposition for cooperation in the presidential poll continue. Akel indicates it favours a candidate of the political "centre".
- The employers and industrialists federation seeks a ban on strikes in essential sectors.
- Right-wing Democratic Rally incumbent leader Yiannakis Matsis will probably run for the post of party chairman again.
- A cabinet reshuffle is expected in the next few days, according to reports of Sigma television station.
